articles.title: LEGO’s SMART Play: Millennium Falcon Set Is Down to Its Lowest Price Yet at Amazon With $20 Discount
articles.summary: Looking to be transported to a galaxy far, far away this fall? LEGO's Star Wars SMART Play: Millennium Falcon can get you there. Well, your minifigures, at least. If you've been hoping to buy this set, which launched earlier this year, Amazon's knocked its price down to $79.95.
body: One very important thing to note about this set, though, is that the LEGO Smart Brick is not included with it. The set is compatible with it, though. So, if you have one of the All-in-One sets, you can use the Smart Brick included in those to get the full effect of hearing the Millennium Falcon and its crew in action.

If you're more interested in the build itself, it looks like an excellent set for Star Wars fans to assemble. Recommended for ages 9 and up, it comes with 885 pieces to create the starship with details like two stud shooters and foldout sections on top that allow you to get a good look at the interior.

Of course, the Millennium Falcon needs a crew, and this set comes with four minifigures to complete it: SMART Han Solo, SMART Chewbacca, SMART Luke Skywalker and SMART C-3PO. As you can tell by the 'SMART' at the front of their names, they can all be paired with the Smart Brick to hear extra sounds as you play. And as for hearing the ship, the set also comes with four SMART Tags.
points: LEGO's Star Wars SMART Play: Millennium Falcon can get you there.

articles.title: Gremlins 3 Gets an Official Teaser, But There's Some Bad News
articles.summary: Gizmo returns to the big screen after decades in the third Gremlins movie, but very little is known about the project. Even though the premiere is still a long way out, Warner Bros. has shared the first teaser for Gremlins 3.
body: Gremlins 3 is the first entry in the series in over 35 years. The last Gremlins movie, Gremlins 2: The New Batch, was released in 1990, six years after Gremlins. While the sequel wasn't as successful as the original Gremlins, the franchise has made millions and amassed thousands of fans in the past four decades. Gremlins has got it all: it's a Christmas movie with horror and comedy elements; there are freaky, but cool-looking creatures that create chaos for the sake of it, and an adorable, fuzzy main character who you just automatically root for.

While animated series based on its lore have been created, what fans have always hoped for is to see the beloved animatronic Gremlins in a third movie. It finally became a reality when Warner Bros. announced Gremlins 3 last year. The announcement included a Nov. 19, 2027, release date. Nearly a year after its announcement, Warner Bros. has now shared a first look at Gremlins 3 with a short teaser, which includes the announcement of a big delay for the movie's release, which will now happen on Oct. 6, 2028.
points: Gizmo returns to the big screen after decades in the third Gremlins movie, but very little is known about the project.

articles.title: 70 Years Later, The Greatest Closing Line In Fantasy History Is Still The Wisest Book Quote Of The 1950s
articles.summary: The fantasy genre is built on unforgettable final acts that leave the stage in a blaze of spectacle. George R.R. Martin famously closes A Game of Thrones by spectacularly reawakening magic with the birth of dragons, while Brandon Sanderson caps the Mistborn trilogy with a universe-altering…
body: Instead of rolling the credits at the coronation of King Aragorn or the collapse of Barad-dûr, Tolkien meticulously winds the narrative down to a deeply personal scale. The hobbits return to liberate the Shire from Saruman's industrialized rot, only for Frodo to realize his psychological wounds are too deep to heal. The true climax isn't a battle, but a farewell. Frodo departs for the Undying Lands from the Grey Havens, leaving Sam behind to inherit Bag End. Sam simply walks back up the hill, opens his green door to his wife Rosie and daughter Elanor, and sits down. Tolkien closes the book with the simple phrase: “'Well, I'm back,' he said.”
points: The fantasy genre is built on unforgettable final acts that leave the stage in a blaze of spectacle.
Instead of rolling the credits at the coronation of King Aragorn or the collapse of Barad-dûr, Tolkien meticulously winds the narrative down to a deeply personal scale.

articles.title: Warner Bros. Pushes Back DC's Dynamic Duo Film, Gremlins 3 Gets One Year Delay
articles.summary: Warner Bros. has pushed back DC's Dynamic Duo and delayed Gremlins 3 by a whole year. Warner Bros. is preparing its 2028 slate, which has resulted in a couple of movies shifting their release dates around.
body: The new Gremlins will be directed by Chris Columbus, who wrote the original Gremlins and helmed classic films like Home Alone. Not much is known about the next film in the franchise, but it's a project Columbus has pursued for over a decade. It will likely be a while longer before we get any more meaningful footage, given it's now two years away from hitting theaters.

DC's experimental Robins movie Dynamic Duo, which will follow Dick Grayson and Jason Todd's early adventures, is also moving its date. The film was originally slated for June 2028, but will now open on September 22, 2028. The film is expected to be a hybrid between traditional CG animation, stop motion, and puppetry, giving it a unique visual style. The Batman director Matt Reeves and current DC Studios boss James Gunn will both produce the film.

It seems like this may be DC's attempt at trying to make something similar to the Spider-Verse films, leveraging younger characters with a unique visual style. Whether there's as much interest in an animated Robins project as there was for a character like Spider-Man remains to be seen.
points: Warner Bros. has pushed back DC's Dynamic Duo and delayed Gremlins 3 by a whole year.

articles.title: J.J. Abrams' Cult Classic "X-Files Meets Buffy" Sci-Fi Series Is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.summary: The early 2000s saw a significant shift in the portrayal of female leads on television. Gone was the one-dimensional damsel-in-distress trope, making space for empowered female protagonists who were allowed to be flawed and multi-dimensional.
body: Buffy Summers from Buffy the Vampire Slayer defined this character template in the late ‘90s, emerging as an iconic and relatable lead who embraced both strength and vulnerability. Lorelai Gilmore ( Gilmore Girls ), Kara “Starbuck” Thrace ( Battlestar Galactic a ), and Veronica Mars ( Veronica Mars ) followed in Buffy’s footsteps, bringing much-needed depth and complexity to female character writing.

Jennifer Garner’s Sydney Bristow from Alias, which ran from 2001 to 2006, is also a part of this wave. Created by J.J. Abrams three years before the genre-defying Lost, Alias was well-received by critics and audiences alike, praised for its unique genre blend and electrifying pacing. If you’ve been meaning to catch up on a somewhat underrated spy thriller series with dazzling action, you’ll be pleased to know that all five seasons of Alias are streaming for free on Pluto TV.

articles.title: YouTube's New A/B Video Test Feature Is Already Creating Fears Over Weaponized Negativity
articles.summary: YouTube is launching a new feature that allows creators to test different cuts of their own videos, leading fans to worry that it could be used for weaponized negativity. Earlier today, YouTube unveiled a bunch of new features coming for creators in 2027.
body: Some have feared that this may encourage creators to test videos that skew positively or negatively before deciding which one gets the most traffic and using that as the permanent choice. One example provided by someone on X is someone making a YouTube video where they review the upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time with a positive and a negative review.

This has also led some to wonder how this might be reflected to viewers. Will some audiences watch completely different videos and be left wondering what others are referring to in the comments or on social media? All in all, the feature poses some flaws, but hopefully YouTube can prevent it from being abused.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering's 10 Best Counterspells, Ranked
articles.summary: Over 30 years of game design, counterspells have evolved from straightforward two-mana hard answers into format-policing safety valves, color-pie-shattering oddities, and zero-mana emergency brakes.
body: Few feelings in Magic: The Gathering rival untapping your blue mana, passing the turn with a full hand, and watching your opponent wonder how many counterspells you’re ready to fire off. Counterspells are more than a defining part of blue’s color identity: They are the ultimate psychological weapon, transforming every spell an opponent casts into a calculated risk.

Separating casual staples from the absolute ceiling of power requires measuring raw mana efficiency, card advantage, and format-warping dominance across Legacy, Vintage, Modern, and Commander. From game-ending tempo swings to free-pitch spells that keep entire competitive formats honest, these are the 10 best counterspells in Magic history, ranked.

Magic is fundamentally defined by the color pie, a rigid set of boundaries dictating what each slice of the spectrum can do. Red is the color of chaotic emotion and aggressive reach, while blue holds a near-monopoly on stack interaction. Tucked away in the game’s earliest sets are the most efficient color-pie breaks in existence, like Red Elemental Blast and Pyroblast. For a single red mana, both cards let you either counter a blue spell or destroy a blue permanent.
points: Over 30 years of game design, counterspells have evolved from straightforward two-mana hard answers into format-policing safety valves, color-pie-shattering oddities, and zero-mana emergency brakes.

articles.title: Discord Begins Rolling Out Age Verification–And A Sponsorship With FanDuel
articles.summary: Discord has officially begun rolling out age-verification measures as of today. The company first announced age verification--and, subsequently, limits placed on accounts of those under 18-- back in February of this year, but delayed a full implementation until just recently.
body: While Discord assures users that "More than 90% of you won’t be asked to confirm your age," the company also acknowledge that their model isn't flawless, and some accounts will need to verify their age to use a non-age-restricted Discord account. If users want to avoid uploading ID or video, they can use services like Apple Pay, Google Play, Google Wallet, or AgeKey, or enter a credit card number.

With any attempt at age verification comes controversy, however, and users of Discord were quick to notice that age verification was rolling out at the exact same time as sponsored ads for sports betting website FanDuel were appearing for American users. Obviously, it's illegal to use FanDuel if you're under 21 (or 18 in some jurisdictions), so it didn't take much for social media users to assume a connection between the two events.

articles.title: Rainbow Six Siege Dev On Competing With GTA 6 And Why There Are No Plans For Siege 2
articles.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 releases this November, and it's expected to take up a lot of time and attention, leading some to worry how other games may fare in its wake.
body: "All of us are going to play it," Mills told The Game Business.

So what can Ubisoft do for Siege when GTA 6 comes out? He said, "It's about being smart and with your expectations so you can keep the team and HQ aligned." He said if the developers working on Siege see the game's player numbers drop, "they can get anxious." However, he observed that the effect on player numbers from a big competitor release is "generally temporary."
Whatever the case, Mills said the "golden rule" that Ubisoft operates by is by serving "the players who stay like kings and queens."
"We don’t go on vacation just because a competitor is swelling the market. We double down and reward those spending their valuable time with us," he said.

articles.title: 30 Years Later, Collecting Pokemon Cards Hits A Little Different
articles.summary: Let me sound like an old for a second. I remember in the late '90s and early '00s, collecting Pokemon cards was a casual hobby. You'd go to your local brick-and-mortar store with the money you made from mowing the lawn or whatever, drop maybe $10 on a couple of packs, rip them open, then go to your…
body: It was so low-key back in the day. Saying that grosses me out, as I sound like a Boomer or Gen Xer, but it's true: Collecting Pokemon cards wasn't that serious, and we didn't put much stock in the cards, stuffing them in bags or pockets and watching them turn up in washing machines.

There have been plenty of incidents involving card collecting and violence lately. Robbers stole over $100,000 in rare cards from a California store in December 2025. A different set of robbers made off with nearly $120,000 in rare cards at gunpoint in New York in January 2026. Police broke up a chaotic Costco scene over Prismatic Evolutions in April 2026. And more recently, a Connecticut man was arrested for assaulting someone in a Target after being confronted for exceeding the store's limit for Pokemon card packs, while a 72-year-old Ohio man pleaded guilty to using a GPS tracker to stalk a woman stocking Pokemon cards.

articles.title: The Industrial Revolution is the reason RPGs have area-of-effect spells: A PC Gamer Causality Chain™
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: Causality Chain is a series at PC Gamer exploring the unlikely links between history, culture, and videogames.

Every time you cast a meteor spell in Diablo 2 or a cloud of daggers in Baldur's Gate 3, you are taking part in a chain of history—a causality chain, if you will—that dates back to the 18th century, when nobody had thought about taking a "warlock dip" since the Salem witch trials. And at that time, it had a very different meaning.

Today we trace the arc of history from the death of the agrarian period, all the way forward to that time you managed to set fire to five goblins at once and felt quite good about how clever you were. We chart the curious contours of cause and effect, and then we put our chins into our hands and we say, "Hmmm. Yes. This is good."
Join us as we tip the dominoes that link the past to the present, then watch the huge and intricate Rube Goldberg machine known as "history" fall over into a heap of discarded playing pieces.

articles.title: High On Life Is Helping Make The Case For Bigger Games On Quest
articles.summary: High on Life has been a big hit since it first launched in 2022, thanks to its bizarre sense of humor, motor-mouthed guns, and polished gameplay. But can it succeed as a virtual reality port?
body: While it's still early days for the project, I took the time to chat to High on Life VR game director Emily O'Neal and Eric Masher, co-founder and chief operating officer for Impact Reality and Flat2VR Studios, about this project and the challenges involved in adapting it for a new platform.

"We want to bring them those high-quality games like High on Life, that [have] more teeth, more depth, and more playability as an actual game. We're not here just for a short snapshot in time; we're here to help grow this industry to where it will be in three to five years from now. Our job and our mission at Flat2VR is to bring the immersive, amazing games that you love playing right now on your console and PC, but bring it to another platform that makes a whole bunch of sense and that feels completely different but still the same.”

Bringing High on Life to VR isn't an easy task either, as you can't just press a "Convert to VR" button for a project of this scale. As O'Neal explained, the original game is massive, and the team is looking to make it run as smoothly as possible on a VR headset.

articles.title: Quake Champions takes a shower, shedding all its 2017 live-service grime and becoming a $10 game
articles.summary: Behold, some wild Quake Champions patch notes. Removed Battle Pass. Removed Weekly / Event Challenges. Removed the Store. Removed Platinum and Shard Currencies. Removed Loot Boxes. Removed Daily Login Rewards.
body: "Today’s update marks a new chapter for Quake Champions as we transition the game from a free-to-play service to a paid application on Steam," the update reads. "Quake Champions is now available for one low price on Steam. No additional content updates are planned at this time. If you previously played Quake Champions on Steam, the new version will appear in your Steam Library at no additional cost."

After nine years, Quake Champions is a live-service game no more: The free-to-play arena shooter is now even more old school as a regular $10 product on Steam. All champions are unlocked from the jump, so you don't have to buy characters piecemeal like way too many games were asking us to do in the mid-2010s. Recently purchased premium currency will be refunded, but if you spent years dropping cash on skins, it might be a little awkward that everybody else now gets those at no additional cost.

videos.summary: Digital Foundry is now fully independent! Join the DF Supporter Program and support the team:
body: Note: Stellar Blade's developer has now confirmed that a frame-gen toggle will be added:

Stellar Blade on Switch 2 uses frame generation to target 60fps - and Capcom is offering the same feature with a toggle in the upcoming Dragon's Dogma 2 port. So how does it work and what have we learned from testing it in Stellar Blade? Beyond that, Tom, Rich and Oliver discuss whether next-gen hardware should be delayed, why Nintendo is avoiding DLSS in its own Switch 2 titles and whether Valve should release an ARM-based handheld. And finally, what's the point of chromatic aberration?
